out.rationale: Bowman et al. describe sandwiching: non-experts try to align a model more capable than them but less capable than experts, who evaluate the result. text: The authors define the weak-to-strong learning problem as how a weak supervisor can oversee a model much smarter than it, and study an analogy that replaces the weak human supervisor with a weak model. Throughout most of the work, a weak supervisor is created by finetuning a small pretrained model on ground truth labels. Its predictions on a held-out set serve as weak labels, and a strong model finetuned on those weak labels is the strong student whose performance is called weak-to-strong performance.
title: Weak-to-strong learning problem and weak supervisor / strong student setup
